findings.problem: InvoiceWorkflow uses String for status and bools for is_validated/is_sent, allowing illegal states such as is_sent=true with status="draft", or is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None. The status string and flag fields are redundant and can contradict each other.
findings.failure_mode: Any code reading the workflow can observe inconsistent lifecycle state, leading to incorrect routing, double-sending, or silent data corruption. No compile-time guarantee prevents invalid transitions.
findings.fix: Replace status String + is_validated bool + is_sent bool with a single InvoiceStatus enum (e.g., Draft, Validated, Sent) that encodes lifecycle invariants. Remove is_sent and is_sent_epoch_ms; instead, store sent_at as Option<Instant> only on the Sent variant.

findings.problem: id is a raw String instead of a typed newtype (e.g., InvoiceId). Domain identifiers should be distinct types to prevent mixing with other string fields.
findings.failure_mode: Accidental misuse of the id field (e.g., comparing with a name, serializing without context) is not caught at compile time. No domain-level validation of id format can be enforced.
findings.fix: Define a newtype struct InvoiceId(String) with a fallible constructor that validates the format, and use it in InvoiceWorkflow instead of String.

findings.problem: All fields of InvoiceWorkflow are pub, exposing the internal representation directly. Domain invariants (even the flawed ones) cannot be enforced through the API surface.
findings.failure_mode: External code can mutate fields directly without going through any transition logic, bypassing validation entirely.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide constructor(s) and transition methods that enforce invariants. Use method receivers with explicit lifecycle gates.

findings.problem: mark_sent accepts any InvoiceWorkflow regardless of its prior state. It unconditionally sets status to "sent" and is_sent to true without checking whether the invoice was validated or is already sent.
findings.failure_mode: An invoice in Draft state can be sent directly, bypassing the validation step. A previously sent invoice can be sent again (idempotency not checked). No transition guards exist.
findings.fix: Define typestates (e.g., InvoiceDraft, InvoiceValidated, InvoiceSent) and have mark_sent take InvoiceValidated, returning InvoiceSent with sent_at_epoch_ms populated. Draft invoices cannot be sent directly.

findings.problem: mark_sent performs mutation by value and returns the modified struct, but has no domain logic separation. The transition logic is mixed into the imperative shell layer.
findings.failure_mode: Cannot be tested as pure logic. Clock/time-dependent behavior (sent_at_epoch_ms) cannot be injected for deterministic testing.
findings.fix: Define a pure function validate_and_send(status: InvoiceValidated, now: u64) -> Result<InvoiceSent, SendError> in the core, keeping I/O and clock concerns in the shell.

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for InvoiceWorkflow lifecycle operations. Marking an invoice as sent is a core business path that should have performance characteristics documented.
findings.failure_mode: No measured evidence that the typestate transition or serialization path meets latency budgets.
findings.fix: Add a microbenchmark for the typestate transition (draft→validated→sent) measuring allocation-free paths.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for invoice lifecycle transitions
no allocation analysis for String-to-newtype conversion paths
no command evidence: no cargo commands run for review
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The core issue is architectural — the entire InvoiceWorkflow type must be replaced with a typestate-enum design before incremental fixes can be validated.
